headline: Autopay Checklist: Six Things to Check Two Days Before Your Bills Leave
sub: Two minutes on the 29th is cheaper than a returned payment on the 1st.
items: Find your next payday, not the next bill.
Read the available balance in the account the bills leave from.
Check which account each bill pulls from.
Compare each amount that varies with last month's.
Subtract. If the result is negative, fix it that day: move money, move a date, or call the biller.
Pick one date each month, two or three days before the busiest one, and put it in your calendar.

headline: How to Change a Bill Due Date: What to Say to the Biller
sub: Most billers can move a due date once a month or so, and some can't, so ask.
items: Move the due date: "I get paid on the 5th. Can you move my due date from the 3rd to the 6th, and does the autopay follow it?"
Amount went up: "My autopay went from $96 to $148. Can you tell me what changed on this bill?"
Pause an autopay: "I'd like the autopay on the 3rd paused so I can pay by hand after the 5th. Will that trigger a late fee?"

headline: Why Autopay Fails Even When Your Balance Looks Fine
sub: The balance is fine and the payment still fails.
items: A new card number, a closed account or an expired card on file can break an autopay.
The payment bounces. A bank can return it unpaid or cover it and charge an overdraft fee, depending on the account.
Card autopay is set to the minimum. It keeps the account current and leaves the rest owing.
Your payday moves. A holiday or a weekend can shift the deposit by a day or two.

headline: What to Say When You Call a Lender About a Missed Payment
sub: Use the number on your statement or the back of the card.

Closing: "Can you read back what we agreed, and can you send it to me in writing? Could I have your name or ID number?"

headline: How Many Days Late Before a Missed Payment Hurts Your Credit?
sub: For most accounts, a payment is reported to Equifax, Experian and TransUnion once it is 30 days past due.
items: Day 1 to 29: a late fee can be added, and interest keeps running on the balance.
Day 30: the lender can report the payment as 30 days late.
Day 60 or more: some card agreements let the lender raise your rate on the existing balance.
Paying before day 30 is what keeps it off the report in the first place.
